summary:
OSTEON is an interactive 3D health visualization platform designed to help astronauts assess and understand skeletal health during long-duration space missions. Inspired by NASA research on musculoskeletal computational modeling and spaceflight-induced bone loss, the project transforms complex biomechanical concepts into an intuitive self-assessment experience.
The platform combines a digital twin of the human skeleton, real-time health indicators, and interactive visualization to demonstrate how exercise contributes to bone maintenance in microgravity environments. Users can explore different skeletal regions, monitor estimated osteogenic stimulus levels, and receive preventive feedback through a clear, color-coded interface.
By supporting astronaut autonomy and simplifying health monitoring, OSTEON addresses one of the key challenges of future lunar, Martian, and deep-space missions: maintaining crew health when communication with Earth may be limited. The project promotes preventive decision-making and makes critical health information more accessible through engaging visual interaction.
details:
OSTEON is an autonomous astronaut health visualization platform focused on skeletal health assessment during long-duration space missions. The project was inspired by NASA research on musculoskeletal computational modeling and the physiological effects of microgravity on the human skeletal system.

The platform combines wearable sensing, local data processing, and an interactive 3D digital twin of the human skeleton to create an intuitive self-assessment experience. Motion data collected from exercise activities is processed through a biomechanical-inspired model that estimates mechanical loading and bone stimulation in key skeletal regions, including the spine, pelvis, femur, and tibia.

OSTEON presents this information through a color-coded 3D skeleton, health indicators, historical trends, and preventive recommendations. Instead of providing medical diagnoses, the system helps astronauts understand whether their exercise routines are generating sufficient mechanical stimulus to support bone maintenance in space.

The platform was designed to operate locally, allowing astronauts to access health information even when communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable. This is particularly important for future lunar, Martian, and deep-space missions, where autonomous health monitoring will become increasingly necessary.

The project was developed using React, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Recharts, FastAPI, SQLite, NumPy, Uvicorn, and PySerial. The hardware architecture was designed around an ESP32 microcontroller and an MPU6050 inertial measurement unit (IMU) to simulate real-world wearable data acquisition.

The creative aspect of OSTEON lies in transforming complex biomechanical and musculoskeletal concepts into an accessible visual experience through an interactive skeletal digital twin. Rather than displaying health metrics as isolated numbers, the system allows users to visually explore different body regions and understand their health status in a more intuitive way.

During development, the team considered astronaut autonomy, usability, communication delays in deep-space missions, scientific credibility, preventive healthcare strategies, and the need to present health information clearly and meaningfully in extreme operational environments.
